question:
A 64-year-old female patient seeks medical attention due to recent changes in her voice and
swallowing difficulties. She discovered an anterior neck mass through self-examination yesterday. She
denies symptoms of anorexia, painful swallowing, weight reduction, or breathing problems. Her medical
history is unremarkable. Her vital signs show a temperature of 37°C (98.7°F), heart rate of 73/min, and
blood pressure of 105/72 mmHg. On physical examination, a solitary, immobile mass is palpated in the
anterior neck region. Which of the following findings would be most indicative of a malignant process in
this case? Answer Choices: (A) Heat intolerance and palpitations (B) Recent upper respiratory tract
infection (C) History of cigarette smoking (D) Recent exposure to ionizing radiation (E) Normal thyroid
stimulating hormone (TSH) level (F) Presence of cervical lymphadenopathy on the contralateral side
(G) Tender neck mass (H) Fluctuating size of the mass with swallowing (I) Neck mass that is cystic and
smaller than 1 cm on ultrasound (J) Family history of autoimmune thyroid disease
 A. Family history of autoimmune thyroid disease
B. Recent exposure to ionizing radiation
C. History of cigarette smoking
D. Heat intolerance and palpitations
E. Fluctuating size of the mass with swallowing
F. Presence of cervical lymphadenopathy on the contralateral side
G. Neck mass that is cystic and smaller than 1 cm on ultrasound
H. Normal thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) level
I. Recent upper respiratory tract infection
J. Tender neck mass
